transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-19
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Maya (Atlas SRE), Liam (Head of ML), Priya (Security)

Summary/Context: quick check-in on Redwood Private (VPC) pilot. Focusing on networking routing, runtime upgrade, perf numbers after quantization, and security docs.

[00:00] Ava: hey everyone thanks for joining for the weekly pilot sync, um we'll go quick like 30 to 45 minutes. jordan and i will lead. quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya: hey maya here, s r e.
[00:10] Liam: liam here, lead ml.
[00:12] Priya: priya, security.
[00:14] Jordan: jordan on the se side, ready to walk through the networking notes.
[00:20] Ava: ok first item - maya you flagged that some worker nodes couldn't reach the control plane after the peering went live, can you summarise?
[00:28] Maya: yeah so after we set up the vpc peering to the redwood VPC, most traffic was fine but a subset of instances in our private-subnet-b couldn't talk to the control plane, packets dropped. we think it's route propagation not enabled on our route table. also noticed nat gateway egress rules that are a bit strict so curl to S3 timed out intermittently.
[00:48] Jordan: that matches what we saw on the pilot logs, connection attempts were hitting the fallback path then timing out, we get a TCP handshake but then it's reset, looks like the route entries were missing. on our side redwood uses a small range for control-plane, we shared the cidr list in the peering doc but maybe the propagate setting wasn't applied.
[01:08] Maya: we used terraform module from our infra team, and it didn't set "enable-route-propagation" for the transit gateway attachment by default. my bad, should've caught it.
[01:18] Jordan: no worries, easy fix. action is to enable propagation or add explicit route table entries for the redwood control-plane cidrs. i'll send exact route entries.
[01:26] Priya: quick question on egress, we have strict outbound rules for compliance, can redwood operate using only HTTPS to our endpoints or does it require other protocols/ports?
[01:36] Jordan: mostly HTTPS (443) and for the runtime we use gRPC over TLS on 443 for control and 8443 for some internal health endpoints. we can tunnel controls via 443 if you prefer. also we can support an HTTP proxy egress if your policies require it.
[01:50] Liam: related, when you say "control plane" what's the expected latency? we observed 80-120ms per request which seems high for small prompts. after the quantization change it dropped a bit but still above our SLA.
[02:04] Ava: good call — jordan do you have the perf numbers from last night's run?
[02:08] Jordan: yeah we ran a batch of 1k short prompts (avg tokens 40) on the v2.1.0 runtime with int8 quantization profile q4_0. median p95 tail latency was 95ms, p99 ~210ms. before the upgrade (v2.0.4) p95 was 130ms, so it's an improvement. however jitter increased on the peered subnets before route fix. the KV / prefix cache hit-rate was 62% which we improved to 78% after bumping cache size.
[02:40] Liam: ok 78% is better, what's causing the remaining misses? prefix mismatch?
[02:44] Jordan: likely prompt tokenization differences and also session pinning across nodes — some requests hit cold KV state because we haven't yet pinned heavy customers to dedicated workers. for the pilot we can pin your top requests to a small pool which should raise hit rate to ~90%.
[02:58] Maya: pinning sounds fine, what about cost implications?
[03:02] Ava: we'll include that in the pricing note — pinning reduces cross-node overhead and lowers token egress but costs some reserved capacity. i'll send numbers.
[03:10] Priya: security side — we still need the audit log example and confirmation about KMS integration. last week you said the private control plane can integrate with our KMS/HSM for key wrapping?
[03:22] Jordan: yes we support customer-managed keys via KMS or an HSM proxy. the control plane encrypts at rest by default with redwood-managed keys but for pilot you can bring keys; we store only wrapped keys. i'll attach the integration doc. note: key rotation in the pilot will require a brief restart of the control-plane service — we'll schedule.
[03:40] Priya: okay also need sample audit logs (S3 path or log format) and retention options for compliance.
[03:46] Ava: i'll drop the audit log sample and retention matrix. expect in the doc pack by 3/21.
[03:52] Liam: another question — the v2.1.0 runtime changed some kernel selection heuristics, we saw minor variance in output (few token outputs changed). Is that expected with quantization?
[04:02] Jordan: yeah quantization + new kernels can change low-probability token generations. we did run evals on your saved prompt set; ROUGE/BLEU differences were negligible for top beams, but there were regressions on a small subset. we can pin you to the older kernel path if you need determinism for the pilot while we tune.
[04:22] Liam: let's do two things: run a regression analysis on the 200-case prompt set and if regressions > 1% we'll pin to the older kernel and continue tuning.
[04:30] Jordan: noted. i'll run that and share the spreadsheet.
[04:34] Maya: ops question — maintenance window for the restart and route change? our ops prefers low-traffic window tuesday 02:00-06:00 UTC. can you do the 4-hour load test then?
[04:44] Ava: yes that's fine from redwood side. we'll do config change at start of window, run the 4-hour load test, and monitor. we'll also push the runtime restart if needed.
[04:52] Priya: please include runbook steps, rollback plan, and expected downtime in the maintenance note.
[04:58] Jordan: will include a step-by-step runbook, healthcheck queries, and rollback instruction (revert route table and restart previous runtime binary).
[05:06] Ava: recap — action items are: jordan to share route entries and ip route dump; maya to enable route propagation and confirm; jordan to run regression analysis and load test; ava to send pricing and security docs. maintenance window tentatively Tue 2025-03-25 02:00-06:00 UTC. any other blockers?
[05:24] Priya: need audit logs and KMS integration doc by 3/21 to present to compliance.
[05:28] Ava: yep we'll get that.
[05:30] Liam: also can we get a quick dashboard link for token-level cost breakdown for the pilot usage?
[05:36] Ava: yes i will provision a read-only dashboard for atlas and share link.
[05:40] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll toggle propagation and report back.
[05:43] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and spreadsheet later today.
[05:46] Ava: cool thanks all, end meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional filler words and slight mis-names, some technical phrases spelled out (e.g., K V cache spelled as "kay vee cache") to reflect ASR quirks.

References/shared artifacts:
- network-peering-checklist.pdf (shared link in email)
- pilot-benchmarks-2025-03-19.xlsx (Jordan will attach)
